items.verbatim_snippet: Cathy Jordan became Chair of the ARH Board of Directors, succeeding the prior Board Chair. Longwoods recorded her transition to Board Chair on July 20, 2021. By September 2021, municipal records also identified Jordan as ARH Board Chair. Her term subsequently ran through 2024.

ARH announced that Leah Levesque would become President and CEO, succeeding Eric Hanna, who was retiring after 13 years as ARH CEO. Levesque had previously been ARH’s VP Patient and Resident Care/CNE and was then VP Patient Care/CNE at Queensway Carleton Hospital. The transition was scheduled for October 1, 2021, with Hanna retiring September 30.

ARH appointed Dr. Florin Padeanu as its new Chief of Staff, effective January 1, 2022, replacing Dr. Christine Schriver after her 11 years in the role. ARH characterized the change as a medical-leadership succession intended to strengthen collaboration and quality of care.

ARH’s June 22, 2023 Board minutes state that a public recruitment process was completed to replace two retiring directors, Erin Stitt-Cavanagh and Bob McGaraughty, plus fill a one-year vacancy. The Board recommended Borys Koba, Rick Holock and Pete Kenny for election, while Oliver Jacob and Colleen MacPhee were recommended for renewed three-year terms. The 2023 by-law change also fixed the Board at 14 members, including four ex-officio, non-voting organizational leaders.

After three years as Board Chair, Cathy Jordan completed her final year as Chair and remained a Board member. Following the 2024 AGM, Oliver Jacob was appointed Chair for a three-year term through June 2027. ARH credited Jordan with helping establish the new Strategic Plan and Integrated Risk Management Framework and guiding the organization through COVID-19, a cyber breach, the CT scanner project and redevelopment planning.

items.verbatim_snippet: Leah Levesque advised the Board in December 2023 that she intended to retire in late June 2024. ARH credited her two-and-a-half-year tenure with the opening of the new Grove Home, Exemplary accreditation, the collaborative Total Knee Program with Queensway Carleton Hospital, expanded surgical services, the Integrated Risk Management Framework and the 2023–2026 Strategic Plan. This announcement launched the CEO succession process.

Following a competitive national search, ARH announced Jeremy Stevenson as its next President and CEO. The Board described Stevenson as an experienced rural-health leader with acute- and long-term-care experience, previously serving as CEO of St. Joseph’s General Hospital Elliot Lake, CEO of the Northeast LHIN and CEO of Mattawa Hospital/Algonquin Nursing Home. He succeeded Levesque after her retirement in 2024.

ARH and Queensway Carleton Hospital announced a joint Chief of Staff model, appointing Dr. Kathi Kovacs to ARH’s Chief of Staff role effective August 1, 2025. Kovacs had been QCH Chief of Staff since 2020. ARH explicitly thanked Dr. Padeanu, who had held the ARH Chief of Staff role since 2022, and said he would continue clinical practice at Tall Pines Clinic and as an ARH hospitalist.

ARH subsequently publicly recognized the three at its AGM, indicating that Jordan’s later Board service ended in 2025 and that MacPhee and McGrath also concluded their Board tenure in 2025. Jordan had served as Chair from 2021–2024.
